# Pitex 1.1.4

Tab and Shift+Tab indent and outdent selected lines. The macOS PDF
preview gains Back and Forward buttons, and builds that cannot start now
say why.

## New

- Tab indents every line of a multi-line selection, and Shift+Tab
  outdents it. The block stays selected, so you can press the key again.
  A selection within one line still types a tab.
- On macOS, the PDF preview has Back and Forward buttons. After a link
  in the PDF moves the view, Back returns to where you were reading.
- On macOS, a setting in Settings > Compile opens the PDF preview in a
  separate window when a project opens. It is off by default.

## Fixes

- On macOS, a build with no TeX engine ends with an error that names the
  folders Pitex searched and how to fix it, instead of looking like a
  build that never finishes.
- The switch that approves running custom commands through a login
  shell stays on when the fallback build command is empty.
- The fallback build command runs when the build-command field is blank,
  as its help text says.
- The build-command help explains the `{file}`, `{filename}` and
  `{outdir}` placeholders. Live compile needs `{outdir}` in a custom
  command.

## Install

Pitex 1.0.0 through 1.1.3 update to 1.1.4 from Settings or, with automatic
installation enabled, at launch. For Homebrew installations, run
`brew update` and `brew upgrade --cask pitex`.

Builds from the earlier 2.x line do not update automatically; install 1.1.4
from the downloads below. Pitex Nightly continues to use its separate
update channel.

## Downloads

Downloads include the macOS ARM64 DMG, Ubuntu 22.04 and 24.04 AMD64 DEBs,
Windows AMD64 installer and portable ZIP, the Ubuntu installer, and
SHA256SUMS.
Windows remains beta.
